Q: Does MarshalByRefObject do anything in .NET (formerly) Core? A:

Love how all the code is inside a big #if FEATURE_REMOTING.

I think the magic-in-CLR part is more in Transparent Proxies.

  • Reflection makes it easy to create the "stub" part of a proxy/stub pair.
  • Creating a proxy for a given interface requires Reflection.Emit.
  • Creating a proxy without an interface, pretending to be another object altogether, is where the magic happens.

Q: Pykd plugin for Windbg not calling breakpoint handler A:

Well I think I've exhausted all avenues and finally got one script to work which is similar to what I added in my original post. I made sure that I was using the 64 bit version of python and the 64 bit version of the pykd extension and same for my program. Previously I was using a 32 bit version of my program.

import pykd

def bp_handler():
    print("Breakpoint hit!")
    reg_name = "rcx"
    value = pykd.reg(reg_name)
    print(f"{reg_name}: 0x{value:x}")
    return False 

try:
    #address_value = pykd.getOffset("ComLineStrcpy!main")
    bp = pykd.setBp(0x000000014000107E, bp_handler)
    print("Breakpoint with callback set")

except Exception as e:
    pykd.dprintln(f"An error occurred: {e}", dml=True)

pykd.go()

Q: flutter_geofire pods error iOS, app runs fine on android but not on iOS A:

This is a version compatibility issue in your dependencies.

The problem

Specifically reading this part from the error message:

flutter_geofire (from `.symlinks/plugins/flutter_geofire/ios`) was resolved to 0.0.1, which depends on
  GeoFire (~> 5.0) was resolved to 5.0.0, which depends on
    GeoFire/Database (= 5.0.0) was resolved to 5.0.0, which depends on
      Firebase/Database (< 12.0.0, > 7.0.0)

This says that the flutter_geofire plugin depends on finding a Firebase/Database version greater than 7 and smaller 12. You're including firebase_database: ^12.1.1, which does not meet those requirements - hence the error message.

Solution

Since there is no newer version of flutter_geofire, you will either have to create one yourself or depend on a lower version of firebase_database - one that geofire is compatible with. I'll go with the latter here, since that's simpler.

If we look up the latest firebase_database version smaller than 12 from the FlutterFire version history on GitHub, that is version 11.3.10 from the July 21, 2025 release of FlutterFire. If we take all the relevant version numbers from there, your Firebase dependencies become:

firebase_core: ^3.15.2
firebase_auth: ^5.7.0
firebase_database: ^11.3.10
firebase_storage: ^12.4.10

So update these version numbers in your pubspec.yaml and you should be good to go.

It might also be a good idea to post a request for a new release to the flutter_geofire repo and/or to submit a PR for it.
